attribution_limitations: Table 2 lists Fbg under the Coagulation test group, but the footnote expands Fbg as fasting blood glucose. The analyte identity is unclear.

The source says these products were required "to reduce the circulatory volume, albumin concentration, and coagulation factors", wording that reads oddly for albumin and plasma products. Whether they were actually administered is also not stated separately.
Adrenaline is described as necessary or required, not explicitly as given with a count or time.

The Introduction states without hedging that the case progressed to cardiac arrest due to a large amount of ascites, but the Discussion hedges the same attribution ("This case suggests", "We should assume"), and the Discussion mechanisms (abdominal compartment syndrome, hypovolemia, impaired cardiac compliance) are general or hedged and not stated as established for this patient.
The Discussion lists a Castleman disease-like lymph node feature as consistent with the criteria, yet also says the lymph node findings only partially met the newer criteria.
The reference point for "the first day" is not named (first day of drainage versus first ICU day), and it is unclear whether 7,300 mL includes the 4,000 mL drained earlier.
The PAIgG unit is printed as "ng/10^(7) calls", a probable print artefact for cells.

HIV and HHV-8 DNA results are merged between the text sentence and Table 2 because the text says all laboratory findings are summarized in Table 2 and both name the same analyte; the text sentence itself has no time.
